title: fix: WARN() → pr_warn() in PBKDF2 backstop in crypto2dev_registry.c
description:
The PBKDF2 backstop in crypto2dev_register_provider() uses WARN() to flag providers that declare min_iterations<1000 or min_salt_len<16. On kernels built with CONFIG_BUG_ON_WARN=y (common on hardened and FIPS kernels), WARN() can halt execution at insmod time, causing the provider to fail loading entirely. The backstop is defense-in-depth only — the framework already enforces the limits in ioctl_do_kdf. A misconfigured provider should warn and load, not crash the module.

Fix: replace the two WARN() calls with pr_warn() and restructure as explicit if-statements.

Location: src/provider/crypto2dev_registry.c:73-80

Found in review WOLFKM-yjf.1.
close_reason: Replaced WARN() with pr_warn() + explicit if-statements; added comment explaining why WARN() was wrong here
